exposure: Post-partum interval (time between giving birth and attempting to conceive again)
cohort: 1489 multiparous women aged 21-45 years, attempting pregnancy with the same male partner for ≤6 menstrual cycles at enrolment, from the Pregnancy Study Online (PRESTO) in the United States and Canada
finding: Among North American pregnancy planners, long post-partum intervals (≥48 months) were associated with slightly reduced fecundability.
mod_finding: Short post-partum intervals (<12 months) were weakly associated with reduced fecundability in some subgroups including women with a history of caesarean delivery.
